narrative.overview:
Development is terrain, not a line. The site is one survey sheet of the first five years: a map-white ground, navy ink for every word, slate contour lines as the sheet's own material, sage woodland and a pale stream as fields, and one dashed teal route with round waymarks running birth to five. The homepage hero is the sheet itself, with an age cursor a parent drags along the route; every inner page carries a stretch of the same sheet (a terrain inset on /tools/, route-segment bars on class rows). The parent is reading a landscape, and the science is the landscape. This replaces the earlier "Seminar" world (Besley, Atkinson Hyperlegible Next, ink bands, amber highlighter, 10px radii), which survives only in the /nsc class app until it is restyled.

The world is calm and inviting but collegiate and respectable (Matthew, 2026-10-13). Nothing is lifted, rounded, washed, or gradiented: fields separate by a tone step, panels announce themselves with a 3px ink rule across the top (a legend bar), photographs sit in a 2px ink frame like map insets, and the one colour that is not a neutral is the teal route. Two inverted navy fields, the office-hours band and the enrol band plus footer, close each page the way the dark field closes a sheet.

Type is Geologica, a wide geometric sans, for display, legend lettering, numerals and buttons, over Literata, an optical-size serif, for everything a tired parent has to read. The pairing reads as a well-made reference map with a printed gazetteer, not a SaaS launch, a clinic, or a nursery.
keyCharacteristics: Map-white ground, navy ink, slate contours, sage woodland, one teal route; no orange, no warm accent at scale.
Geologica 600 display with tight tracking over Literata 400 at 17px.
Square corners everywhere (every radius token is 0); no box-shadow at rest.
3px ink rules as legend bars on panels, lists and figures; 6px colour bars as route segments on legend cells and class rows; 2px ink frames on photographs.
One phrase mark per headline: a patch of woodland behind the words, the same ink.
Full light/dark theming via [data-theme]; on the night sheet the ground stays lighter than the navy fields so the band structure survives and the route brightens.
One signature interaction: the age cursor on the route; the route draws in once on load.

rules.name: The One Route Rule
rules.body: Teal is the only chromatic colour at text or button size. Anything that asks for the eye (a button, a link, the active waymark, the open chip's text) is teal; anything that does not is ink, a grey, or a field. If a second accent appears, the map has lost its route.

rules.name: The No Orange Rule
rules.body: Orange, amber and terracotta are never a main colour (Matthew, 2026-10-13). The legacy --amber* names still exist in tokens-terrain.css but resolve to the route and its tint; do not reintroduce a warm value under them. The arcade's isolated cabinet palettes are the one exception and stay on /arcade.

rules.name: The Night Sheet Rule
rules.body: In dark mode the ground (#141E28) stays lighter than the navy fields (#0F171F, #0A1016), contours dim to #45596C, and the route brightens to #7FC4BC with #07211E text on it.

rules.name: The Legend Hand Rule
rules.body: Geologica is the hand for anything that labels, counts or acts; Literata is the hand for anything that explains. A number in Literata or a paragraph in Geologica is a mistake.

rules.name: The Label Under the Title Rule
rules.body: Headings never carry a kicker, eyebrow or numeral above them. A class's label ("Class 2: language, autonomy, and big feelings") sits under its title in the map-label voice. Status and meta go beside or below, never above.

rules.name: The One Phrase Rule
rules.body: The .hl mark (woodland behind the words, same ink; ink-700 with white text on navy) is the one typographic flourish: at most one phrase per page-level headline, never on every heading.

rules.name: The Flat Sheet Rule
rules.body: A surface is a tone step and a legend bar, never a lift. If a new element needs a shadow, it is a floating menu or it is wrong.

dos: Do keep the map-white sheet as the ground and separate sections by a tone step (bg → bg-alt → surface), never by a hairline.
Do mark a panel with a 3px ink rule across its top and a class row or legend cell with a 6px route bar (slate at rest, teal when active).
Do use teal for every action and nothing else (The One Route Rule); hover is a deeper teal or an inverted fill, never a lift.
Do set labels, numerals, buttons and legends in Geologica and running text in Literata (The Legend Hand Rule), with tabular numerals wherever numbers align.
Do frame photographs as square insets with a 2px ink border and no filter, and reach for a captioned figure or a terrain inset before a photograph when the section explains something.
Do keep every SVG figure and the sheet accessible: <title>, <desc>, a visible caption, a real range input for the cursor, dash patterns as well as colour.
Do honour prefers-reduced-motion, keep content visible by default, and keep the theme toggle working on every surface.
donts: Don't use orange, amber or terracotta as a main colour, or any warm fill larger than an error message (The No Orange Rule).
Don't round a corner, add a box-shadow at rest, lift a button on hover, or wash a hero with a gradient or graph paper (The Flat Sheet Rule).
Don't put a kicker, eyebrow, numeral or status above a heading; the class label sits under the title (The Label Under the Title Rule).
Don't put the phrase mark on more than one headline per page, or use it for a colour other than woodland on light and ink-700 on navy.
Don't go clinical or nursery: no hospital-blue, no pastels, no stock-baby imagery, no deficit framing in the readout copy.
Don't use border-left or border-right as a coloured accent stripe; the only coloured bars run along the top.
Don't animate layout properties; use transform, opacity, and stroke-dashoffset, on the house ease cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1).
Don't restyle .site-header or .site-footer outside chrome.css, or bring a Seminar value (Besley, amber, 10px radii) back from the nsc app.
